data.description:
## Goal

Make the bounded contention queue cover requests denied by the **prefill-aware guard**, not just requests denied by the generating-only pool, so prefill-saturated requests wait for a slot instead of falling back to remote.

## Problem (code-inspection finding)

Two different occupancy gates decide whether a local dispatch happens:

1. **provider.py in-front-of-router check** (`_local_concurrency_info` → `_get_local_concurrency_info`): returns the **generating-only** count.
   ```python
   cur_local, max_local = _local_concurrency_info(config, endpoint=local_endpoint)
   if cur_local >= max_local:
       _maybe_queue_for_local_slot(...)   # queue engages
   ```
2. **router.py dispatch-lease check** (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`): denies on EITHER
   ```python
   if _generating_count >= max_local: return (False, ...)
   if _prefill_count >= max_local:    return (False, ...)   # <-- prefill gate
   ```

The contention queue's wake predicate only watches the **generating** count:
```python
slot_free_check=lambda: _get_local_concurrency_info(config)[0] < max_local
```

So a request that arrives while a **prefill** is in flight (prefill_count >= max_local, generating_count == 0) passes the provider.py check without queueing, reaches the router, is denied by the prefill gate, and returns HTTP 503 `local_lease_active` → immediate remote fallback.

## Evidence (24h window 2026-09-15 13:49 → 2026-09-16 13:49)

- `local_dispatch_denied` events: 449 (active=1: 373, active=2: 65, active=3: 11)
- `Fallback triggered reason=local_lease_active`: **425** (all fast mode; cheap mode = 0 because cheap has 3 slots and its queue absorbs contention)
- `contention_queue_dispatch`: 1,757 events, median wait **0.00s**, p99 11.4s, max 33.7s, total wait only 498s
- `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`: **6** events (all at the 45s fast cap)

The near-match between deny count (449) and lease-active fallbacks (425), combined with zero `fallback_after_queue` in fast mode beyond the 6 cap-hit cases, indicates most denials never entered the queue — consistent with the prefill gate firing while the generating count was 0.

## Why it matters

Each `local_lease_active` fallback is a request served remotely while the local slot was NOT generating — i.e. capacity the local model could have used. Converting them to local work raises local busy time and cuts remote spend. (Note: prefill is GPU work, so this is not "idle GPU" — but it is serializable work the queue currently discards.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The contention queue wake predicate accounts for the prefill-in-flight count, not only the generating count (either by including `_prefill_count` in `slot_free_check`, or by having the router route prefill-gate denials into the queue).
- [ ] A request denied solely by the prefill gate waits (bounded by `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) and is dispatched local when the prefill completes, instead of returning `local_lease_active`.
- [ ] Queue wait is still subtracted from the adaptive timeout budget (existing Q2=a contract).
- [ ] Long-prefill guard preserved: the queue must not admit more concurrent prefills than `session_slot_pool_size` (i.e. it must not defeat the prefill-aware guard).
- [ ] Metrics/logging distinguish generating-saturation waits from prefill-saturation waits.
- [ ] Tests cover: prefill-saturated request queues and dispatches; prefill-saturated request exceeding the cap falls back as `fallback_after_queue`.
- [ ] Full test suite green.

## Open question to resolve first

Quantify how many of the 425 fallbacks would have succeeded within the wait cap (i.e. prefill completing within 45s). Large prefills (>45s) will still fall back, so the benefit is bounded by the prefill-duration distribution. Measure before/after on a 24h window.

## Related

- LP-0MTH7JX82000YS5N (generating-only pool + prefill-aware guard — completed; this closes the gap it left)
- LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D (contention queue — policy/caps)
- LP-0MU1S617L002Q9PR (parent: large-context sessions stall/time out)
data.title: Contention queue ignores prefill-saturated dispatches (fast-mode local_lease_active fallbacks bypass the queue)

# Epic: Overnight remote-chain exhaustion — accurate diagnostics, quarantine visibility, bounded chain-hold

## Problem statement

During the overnight UTC gaps (01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00) every remote provider in the
`plan`/`author`/`code` fallback chains is outside its configured `available_times` window, and the
only always-on provider (`local-qwen3`) is refused by the router for oversized/uncompactable
sessions. The chain then exhausts and the proxy returns a 503 whose prose blames the schedule even
when the dominant blockers were usage-limit quarantine and a failed compaction summarizer; clients
do not recognise the wording (`Unrecognized error:`), and the request is held for up to
`chain_hold_seconds × chain_hold_max_cycles` (15 minutes) before the failure surfaces. The result
is a misleading error, invisible quarantine state, and avoidable latency on an unattended
overnight path.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call engineer** — must tell a genuine out-of-hours gap apart from a
  usage-limit quarantine, a local-capacity (lease) block, or a failed compaction summarizer from a
  single diagnostic line or response body.
- **Local agent (herdr worker / Pi session)** — needs a terminal, machine-readable error with an
  accurate `Retry-After` so it can back off or queue instead of waiting ~15 minutes and then
  surfacing `Unrecognized error:`.
- **Downstream observability (`proxy-usage-analysis`)** — needs chain-hold cycle re-emissions to be
  distinguishable from genuine new client demand so fallback/demand counters are not inflated.

Example user stories:

- As a proxy operator, I want exhaustion diagnostics to name every blocker (time window, usage-limit
  quarantine, local slot) with its remaining time, so I can explain an overnight failure without
  grepping raw logs.
- As a client agent, I want a stable machine-readable exhaustion code and a truthful `Retry-After`,
  so my recovery classifier can retry or queue rather than surface `Unrecognized error:`.
- As the proxy, I want the chain-hold to wait no longer than the real time until a provider can serve
  the request, so I never add 15 minutes of pointless latency.
- As a local agent competing for the single slot, I want a local lease denial to queue for the slot
  before falling through to a remote chain that cannot serve me, so my request is not silently held.

## Context

Overnight (local 02:00–05:00 and 07:00–11:00 = **UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00**), remote-only
fallback chains exhaust. Every remote tier in the `plan`/`author`/`code` chains is gated by
`available_times`, and the only always-on provider (`local-qwen3`) is refused by the router for
oversized/uncompactable sessions (`_route_remote_with_compaction_guidance`,
`proxy/proxy/router.py:681`). The proxy then returns a 503 whose text is:

    All providers unavailable: no provider is available during the current scheduled time window

That message is wrong (the dominant blockers were usage-limit quarantine and a failed compaction
summarizer) and is not matched by the client recovery classifier, producing `Unrecognized error:`.

## Evidence (2026-09-16/17)

- Config: `proxy/config.yaml:268` and siblings — `available_times: ["00:00-01:00","04:00-06:00","10:00-00:00"]`
  leaves UTC gaps 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00.
- `proxy.log.2026-09-16_01` @ 02:20 local:
  `compaction_remote_with_guidance ... refusing local near-full-slot dispatch` →
  `Skipping opencode-go-3/-2: usage_limit_reset_pending` →
  `Skipping opencode-go/deepseek-flash: outside its available_times window` →
  `All providers exhausted ... unavailable={}` → `Chain exhausted ... holding 300s (cycle=0, max_cycles=3)`.
- Exhaustion events by hour cluster exactly in the two UTC gaps; ~0 outside them.
- 2026-09-17 09:03 UTC: a further variant — local dispatch lease held by another session
  (`local_dispatch_denied`), all remotes out of window, queue policy bypassed, silent multi-cycle
  hold and no `*-response.json` recorded for the client.

## Desired change

Decompose the fix into the child work items below; each child carries its own measurable acceptance
criteria. At the epic level the outcome is: overnight exhaustion is diagnosed truthfully, quarantine
and local-capacity causes are visible, the hold is bounded by real availability, and clients receive
a stable machine-readable error.

## Children

1. **LP-0MU56ZFII004L7OO** (bug, high) — time-window-specific 503 only when **every** provider was
   window-skipped; otherwise the generic exhaustion response with diagnostics.
2. **LP-0MU56ZFVD001LP0H** (bug, high) — expose usage-limit quarantine in exhaustion diagnostics and
   derive `retry_after` from the soonest real availability.
3. **LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08** (feature, medium) — bound chain-hold by the real `retry_after`.
4. **LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G** (feature, high) — stable machine-readable exhaustion error code for
   client classification.
5. **LP-0MU5AIAAY003KVM0** (bug, high) — chain-hold cycles re-run provider resolution but never
   re-run session handling/compaction; make the semantics explicit and re-emissions observable.
6. **LP-0MU5BOMJM008F17C** (bug, high) — local lease denial should queue for the local slot before
   falling through to a remote chain that cannot serve it, and must yield a terminal error.

The original 4 epic deliverables map onto children 1–4; children 5 and 6 were discovered during the
2026-09-17 investigation of the same failure domain and are included in the epic scope.

## Definition of done

Detailed acceptance criteria live in the child work items (this epic is an umbrella; the coverage
gate treats a parent without its own AC section as fully covered by its children). The epic is done
when:

- Every child above is terminal and its own acceptance criteria are satisfied.
- An end-to-end overnight-gap scenario shows an accurate 503 (true cause, quarantine visible,
  `Retry-After` consistent, stable code) and no hold longer than real availability.
- The change is covered by automated tests in the proxy suite and the full project test suite passes.
- Operator-facing documentation (config comments, proxy docs, runbooks) is updated.

## Constraints

- Must preserve existing short-cooldown behaviour (bounded `chain_hold_max_cycles`) and the existing
  `all providers exhausted` / `no provider available` client-recognition contract while adding the
  new machine-readable discriminator.
- Must not wake or bypass `available_times`; the schedule is intentional cost/availability policy.
- Must not kill or restart the proxy as part of the fix; changes ship through the normal test/build
  workflow.
- Client-side classifier changes live in ContextHub (separate repository / work item), not here.

## Existing state

- `_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:2696`) fires whenever
  `not any_provider_tried and not unavailable and any(attempt.status == "outside_time_window")`; it
  does not consider usage-limit quarantine or local/compaction skips.
- `_log_exhausted_providers` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:4305`) only inspects entry-name and brand
  cooldowns, so `_usage_reset_at` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:90`) quarantines are invisible and the
  payload is `unavailable={}`.
- `_providers_outside_window` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:2088`) checks only
  `_is_within_allowed_window`, so a quarantined-and-out-of-window provider is reported as
  `outside_time_window`.
- `_run_chain_cycles` holds for `server.chain_hold_seconds` (300) × `server.chain_hold_max_cycles`
  (3) independent of `_compute_retry_after` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:2045`).
- The local dispatch gate returns a synthetic `503 reason=local_lease_active`
  (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:1433`; logged at
  `proxy/proxy/router.py:1087`) which is treated as a retryable provider failure, bypassing the
  configured contention-queue policy.
- Config: `proxy/config.yaml:575,579` (`chain_hold_*`), `proxy/config-cheap.yaml:752,761`
  (`contention_queue_policy: queue`, `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 120`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — exhaustion response builders, diagnostics, chain-hold cycles,
  `retry_after` computation, local-lease classification.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — local dispatch gate and compaction-guidance routing.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — local dispatch lease acquisition / contention-queue path.
- `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — `available_times`, `chain_hold_*`,
  `contention_queue_*`.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`, `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue*.py` — regression coverage per child.
- `docs/dev/` proxy docs / runbook — operator-facing diagnostics documentation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Naive coverage matcher.** The shared tree-coverage helper matches parent to child ACs by token
  overlap; umbrella epic criteria do not match, so the epic uses a `Definition of done` section and
  relies on the supported parent-without-AC coverage path.
- **Assumption:** the `available_times` schedule is intentional and must not be widened as part of
  this epic (the fix is diagnosability and boundedness, not availability policy).
- **Assumption:** client-side recovery classification is owned by ContextHub and tracked separately
  (WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W / WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK).
- **Failure mode:** a stable `code` field must not remove or change the existing `error` prose that
  older clients recognise; additive-only contract.
- **Failure mode:** bounding the hold must not strand genuine short-cooldown recoveries; tests must
  cover small/medium/large `retry_after`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the compaction RCA (LP-0MU570JAA006LMID) was deleted and successor work
  exists (e.g. LP-0MU5Y9CO2002L4L5); summarizer-quality fixes are tracked there and are **out of
  scope** for this epic rather than being pulled in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Does this epic need a numbered acceptance-criteria list of its own, or is the children's AC
  set sufficient?** — Answer (agent, no producer input required): the epic is an umbrella; detailed
  ACs live in the six children and the shared coverage helper treats a parent without an AC section
  as fully covered by its children. The epic states a `Definition of done` closure condition
  instead. Source: `shared/tree_coverage.py` `test_parent_without_ac_section`.
- **Q: Is the `available_times` schedule itself in scope (i.e. should the gaps be removed)?** —
  Answer (agent, from supplied context): no. The schedule is intentional cost/availability policy;
  the epic covers diagnostics, visibility and bounded worst-case latency only. Source: epic context.
- **Q: Is the deleted compaction RCA still a dependency?** — Answer (agent, verified via `wl`): the
  RCA item LP-0MU570JAA006LMID was deleted; successor compaction work is tracked separately and is
  referenced as out-of-scope context, not as a blocking dependency. Source: `wl show
  LP-0MU570JAA006LMID`.
- **Q: Are the referenced code paths still current after recent changes?** — Answer (agent, verified
  2026-09-26): yes. The window-specific builder still ignores quarantine/local skips, the diagnostics
  logger still omits `_usage_reset_at`, and the hold is still independent of `retry_after`; line
  numbers were refreshed during intake. Source: repository inspection of `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.

## Related

- LP-0MS4ETBNO0022QAC (Add timed access to models), LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4 (Honest Retry-After),
  LP-0MU1RXEPL005CK97 (remote tier stalls), LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ (GoUsageLimitError reset),
  LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW (usage-limit quarantine keying), LP-0MSH94Z7K007VKC9 (chain-hold feature),
  LP-0MU5Y9CO2002L4L5 (summarizer token budget — out of scope).
- Client-side follow-up: WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W, WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK (ContextHub recovery classifier).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSUDM0V40052HPR** – [HIGH] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/skill/cleanup/scripts/delete_remote_branches.py:13 — Module level import not at top of file (E402) (completed)

- **LP-0MSDRRDWK009QT4E** – Recovery-first silent continue for pre-content mid-stream failures (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 300s, access, accurate, alongside, always (+88 more)

# Chain-hold: bound hold duration by the real retry_after

**Parent:** LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO

## Problem

`_run_chain_cycles` holds an exhausted request for
`server.chain_hold_seconds` (300) × `server.chain_hold_max_cycles` (3) = **15 minutes** and then
returns the exhaustion response, independent of when a provider can actually become available.
During the overnight `available_times` gaps nothing can recover for hours, so the hold is pure
added latency before the client sees the failure. Conversely, a short cooldown (e.g. 2 min) is
over-held.

## Change

Bound the hold by the computed `retry_after`:

- If `retry_after` is within the hold budget, hold at most that long (or the configured hold,
  whichever is smaller).
- If `retry_after` exceeds the budget (or a configured maximum), return the exhaustion response
  immediately with an accurate `Retry-After` rather than holding through cycles that cannot
  succeed.
- Preserve current behaviour for the common short-cooldown case (bounded cycles).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chain-hold never waits longer than the computed `retry_after`.
- [ ] When `retry_after` is large (window/usage-limit reset), the response is returned without
      exhausting all `chain_hold_max_cycles`.
- [ ] Streaming clients still receive periodic `: chain exhausted (...)` feedback during any hold.
- [ ] Tests assert hold duration tracks `retry_after` for small, medium and large values.

## References

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` `_run_chain_cycles` / chain-hold section (LP-0MSH94Z7K007VKC9)
- `proxy/config.yaml`: `chain_hold_seconds: 300`, `chain_hold_max_cycles: 3`
data.title: Chain-hold: bound hold duration by the real retry_after

# Startup-ramp 503: include the ramp end time in the response

## Goal

As an operator (or client implementer) receiving the post-restart
`503 startup_ramp` response, I want to know **when** the ramp ends - both as an
absolute timestamp and as seconds remaining - so I can wait exactly long enough
instead of inferring it from the jittered `Retry-After`.

## Context

`_do_proxy_openai_api` in `proxy/proxy/ui.py` (part of the uncommitted startup
ramp, comments reference LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX) currently returns:

```
HTTP 503
Retry-After: <randomized jitter in [jitter_min, jitter_max] + 3s margin>
body: {"error":{"type":"startup_ramp","code":"startup_ramp",
                "message":"Server is starting up; retry shortly."},
       "status":503,"retry_after":N}
```

The `message` gives no indication of how long the ramp lasts, and `retry_after`
is only the (jittered) per-attempt delay - not the time until the gate lifts.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: The `startup_ramp` response body includes the absolute time the ramp
  ends, ISO-8601 UTC (e.g. `"ramp_ends_at": "2026-09-20T16:14:28Z"`).
- **AC2**: The body includes seconds remaining until the gate lifts
  (e.g. `"ramp_remaining_seconds": 6`), distinct from the jittered
  `retry_after`.
- **AC3**: The human-readable `message` states when the ramp ends and/or the
  seconds remaining.
- **AC4**: `Retry-After` / `retry_after` semantics are unchanged (still
  randomized jitter in `[jitter_min, jitter_max]` + margin).
- **AC5**: Tests in `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py` assert the new fields are
  present and internally consistent (`ramp_ends_at` ~= now + remaining) while
  the gate is active; existing tests stay green.
- **AC6**: `/skill:test` full suite green.

## Notes / blockers

- The startup-ramp feature is currently **uncommitted in the main checkout**
  (`proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/proxy/mode.py`, `proxy/proxy/server.py`,
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` modified; `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py` untracked) and
  references a placeholder id `LP-0MUA6RAMP001XXXX`. Implementation must happen
  in a worktree (implement skill), so this uncommitted state must be resolved
  (committed to a branch/worktree, with operator permission) before the
  enhancement can be implemented cleanly.
- `Retry-After` is computed from `time.monotonic()`; the absolute end time must
  be derived from wall-clock (`time.time() + remaining`) and formatted as UTC.
data.title: Startup-ramp 503: include the ramp end time in the response

## Fixed in LP-0MUBDKDFG002W221 (commit 3cf3616a)

Root cause: test-isolation false positive. The assertion `assert "proxy/proxy/scripts" not in checked` is a raw substring check over the absolute path. When the repo/worktree root itself ends in `proxy` (this worktree: `.../wl-LP-0MUBDKDFG002W221-medium-home-rgardler-projects-llm-proxy`), the legitimate resolved path `<root>/proxy/scripts/start-qwentts.sh` contains the substring `proxy/proxy/scripts`, failing spuriously. On the main checkout (root `/home/rgardler/projects/llm`) the same code passes, so this only surfaced inside a `-proxy`-suffixed worktree.

Fix: replaced the brittle substring check with an exact repo-root-relative comparison:

```python
repo_root = os.path.dirname(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
)
rel = os.path.relpath(checked, repo_root)
assert rel == os.path.join("proxy", "scripts", "start-qwentts.sh"), (
    f"Expected path relative to repo root to be "
    f"'proxy/scripts/start-qwentts.sh', got {rel!r}"
)
```

This preserves the regression guard (a duplicated `proxy/proxy/scripts` resolution would yield a different relative path) while being independent of the absolute checkout location.

Verification:
- `pytest tests/test_lifecycle_spawn.py` → 25 passed (from the `-proxy` worktree that previously failed).
- Full suite green in the LP-0MUBDKDFG002W221 gate.

ACA: the test now passes against latest `dev` regardless of the repo-root directory name.
